newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Slovak bank VUB says lower profit good result.
newsitem.headline: Slovak bank VUB says lower profit good result.

text.p: Gross profit at VUB a.s., Slovakia's largest commercial bank, fell sharply in 1996, but bank officials said they were satisfied with the result which included heavy provisioning for its loan portfolio.
VUB on Friday said its pre-tax profit fell to 79.6 million crowns ($2.4 million) from 2.91 billion crown profit in 1995, as it created some 1.5 billion crowns in reserves for classified loans.
"We consider the result satisfactory since our main priority was to continue the restructuring of our loan portfolio," VUB Vice-president Dusan Paulik told a news conference.

"The planned pre-tax profit was some 75 million crowns, so the final figure was fully in line with our policy which has a target to decrease deficit of sources for covering risky assets," he adding the bank still needed to create reserves of 7.8 billion crowns.

Paulik said the bank's proportion of non-performing loans -- which decreased by 4.7 billion crowns in 1996 to some 40 billion crowns -- was brought lower mainly by more effective execution of property deposited for credits.
The overall volume of credits on VUB's books totalled 110 billion crowns at the end of last year. The bank accounts for about 33 percent of the entire amount of credits extended in Slovakia.
"You have to put the bad loans in the right perspective, since our bank inherited two-thirds of its risky assets from the communist Czechoslovak state bank," Paulik said.
VUB inherited the risky assets as part of the split of the former Czechoslovakia in 1993.

VUB's capital adequacy ratio was 7.33 percent as of December 31, 1996, but the bank achieved the figure due to some "unspecified exemptions" from central bank (NBS) criteria for fulfilment of the measure, Paulik said.
"This year (1997) will be much more difficult concerning the capital adequacy since the NBS will no longer accept any exeptions for fulfilment of the criteria," Paulik said.

The NBS target for VUB's capital adequacy ratio without the exemptions is 4.18 percent for the first quarter of 1997, and the central bank will gradually increase the required ratio for VUB to 6.2 percent by the end of this year.
The NBS has demanded a capital adequacy ratio of 8.0 percent for all banks.
VUB's balance sheet total increased by 11 billion crowns last year to 181.5 billion crowns.

VUB is one of the two largest commercial banks -- together with IRB bank -- which is allowed to be privatised, though it is still controlled by state through its privatisation agency, the National Property Fund (NPF). The NPF holds 50.799 percent in VUB.
